title: Is Workato Free? Pricing and Alternatives for 2026
summary: Is Workato free? No — Workato doesn't offer a free plan, but several cheaper automation alternatives are available.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits as a Workato alternative


You can test a lighter tool without a purchase order, and[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) gives you a free hosted account and lets you run the same MIT-licensed core on your own server.


Its free cloud plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month, unlimited flows and up to 5 users, as listed on its pricing page, so anyone consuming more than 1,000 credits monthly or adding a 6th user has exhausted the free tier.


The core is MIT-licensed, with the licence file in the GitHub repository, and the 750 integrations can be counted in that repository's community integrations directory, so you can connect to most platforms without custom development.


Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production, **so it's both deployed and open** .


In the illustration below, a hosted cloud workspace with a flow of connected steps sits beside a team's own server running the same open-source flow. A shelf of integration blocks feeds each.


What to take from it is that the flow's the same either way. Only who runs the machine changes.


### What the free tier and self-hosting include


In Activepieces' terms, a flow's an automation: a trigger followed by steps. Each step uses an integration, which is a connector to an app or a built-in utility. The cloud free tier lets you build flows in a hosted workspace without installing anything.


If you self-host, you run the open-source edition from the project's repository and docs, on infrastructure you control. That costs you server time and maintenance, and it removes the vendor's task cap from the picture.


If a connector's missing, you or a contractor can write one in TypeScript and add it to your own instance, because the integrations are open source too. That's a path Workato's closed connector model doesn't offer.


### Where the Activepieces free tier falls short


Governance is the first gap. Workato's built around controlled promotion between environments, detailed audit trails and role-based access for large teams.


At that depth, Activepieces' free and community offerings don't match. If an auditor will ask who changed a recipe and when, you'll be asking your own team to build that answer.


The connector catalogue's smaller. Before you commit, open the integration list and look for the exact action you need, not just the app's name. An app listed with a trigger but no "update record" action's a common way a migration stalls.


When a flow fails at month end, nobody's contractually obliged to answer. Support is the third gap. Self-hosting means you're the on-call team, and community channels aren't a service agreement.


### Which Workato workloads it suits and which it does not


It suits simple, linear work: moving a form submission into a spreadsheet, posting a notification when a deal changes stage, or syncing a small number of records on a schedule. These are the flows that a two-week trial can prove or disprove.


It doesn't suit heavy enterprise integration. That means long-running transactions across several core systems, strict separation of development and production, or compliance rules that demand vendor-backed support.


If your Workato use looks like that, a free tier's the wrong test, and the honest answer to "do I need Workato?" may be yes.
